_notes: Hand-checked answer key for the jewellery real-world validation slice (jewellery_retail_transactions.md). Unlike the F&B/CNC slices, these questions test PRICING PLAUSIBILITY against real transaction data, not document faithfulness -- there is no narrative text here for Tanya to retrieve chunks from in the usual RAG sense. Use these as direct lookups/comparisons against the table, not as retrieval questions for the chunk-embed-retrieve pipeline.

questions.question: What is the real median price of a gold pendant with a stated gem, and how does TGMOK Holdings' example custom pendant quote compare?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Real median gold+gem pendant price: $136.85 (n=9,110). TGMOK's custom quote (JWL-Q-3391) totals $2,029.92 -- about 15x the real median, though it includes an $850 one-time die-tooling charge a mass-market pendant wouldn't carry.

questions.question: Which jewellery category has the widest real price range, and what does that suggest about pricing a single 'typical' item?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Earrings: $30.00 to $34,448.60 (n=23,889) -- the widest range of any category. A single point estimate ('a gold earring costs $X') is not meaningful without specifying gem/complexity, similar to how TGMOK's own pricing policy varies workmanship margin 12-28% by design complexity.

questions.question: Is silver jewellery common in this real dataset, or is gold dominant?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Gold dominates heavily: 89,082 gold rows vs 1,365 silver and 2 platinum, out of ~90,559 priced rows. TGMOK Holdings' jewellery division is described as gold-focused, which is broadly consistent with this real market's composition (though this dataset is one retailer, not a market-wide claim).

questions.question: What was the average delivery time for jewellery orders in this dataset?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Not covered -- this dataset has no shipping/delivery/fulfilment fields, only event_time, order/product/category ids, quantity, price, and product attributes (colour, metal, gem). Tanya should say this isn't in the data rather than guessing a delivery time.
